parameters.cypherQuery:
=MERGE (
  s:Supplier {
    id: '{{ $json.id }}' 
  }
)
ON CREATE SET 
  s.name = '{{ $json.name }}',
  s.country = '{{ $json.country }}',
  s.lead_time_days = toInteger({{ $json.lead_time_days }}),
  s.quality_score = toFloat({{ $json.quality_score }}),
  s.created_at = datetime()
ON MATCH SET 
  s.name = '{{ $json.name }}',
  s.country = '{{ $json.country }}',
  s.lead_time_days = toInteger({{ $json.lead_time_days }}),
  s.quality_score = toFloat({{ $json.quality_score }}),
  s.updated_at = datetime()
RETURN s.id AS created_id

=MERGE (
  m:Material { 
    material_id: '{{ $json.material_id }}' 
  }
)
SET 
  m.material_name = '{{ $json.material_name }}',
  m.material_type = '{{ $json.material_type }}',
  m.cost_eur = toFloat({{ $json.cost_eur }}),
  m.ingested_at = datetime('{{ $json.ingested_at }}')
RETURN m.material_id AS created_id

=MERGE (
  cs:ChargingStation { unit_id: '{{ $json.unit_id }}' }
)
SET 
  cs.serial_number = '{{ $json.serial_number }}',
  cs.model = '{{ $json.model }}',
  cs.country = '{{ $json.country }}',
  cs.installation_site = '{{ $json.installation_site }}',
  cs.installation_date = date('{{ $json.installation_date }}'),
  cs.ingested_at = datetime('{{ $now.toISO() }}')
WITH cs
MATCH (
  l:Location {
    country: '{{ $json.country }}'
  }
)
MERGE (cs)-[:LOCATED_IN]->(l)
RETURN cs.unit_id AS created_unit, l.location_code AS location_code

parameters.text:
=You are a precise supply chain knowledge graph entity extractor. Analyze the document below and extract ALL entities and relationships.

DOCUMENT ({{ $json.fileName }}):
{{ $json.content }}

IMPORTANT ENTITY RESOLUTION RULES:
1. CANONICAL IDs: You MUST use these exact IDs for known actors: A1=Steel Supplier Alpha, A2=Plastic Materials Corp, A3=Asian Injection Molding, A4=Global Sea Freight, A5=Electronics Manufacturing, A6=Certified Cable Works, A7=Industrial Coating GmbH, A8=EuroCharge Assembly, A9=VDE Testing Services, A10=TransLogistics EU, A11=Civil Works Services, A12=Installation Partners, A13=EuroCharge Network, A14=Field Maintenance Pro, A15=European Recycling, A16=Materials Recovery Inc, A17=Waste Management EU
2. LOCATIONS: Use LOC_GER=Germany, LOC_IND=India, LOC_VIE=Vietnam, LOC_SIN=Singapore, LOC_CZE=Czech Republic, LOC_POL=Poland, LOC_HUN=Hungary, LOC_BEL=Belgium, LOC_NET=Netherlands, LOC_FRA=France, LOC_AUT=Austria, LOC_SWI=Switzerland, LOC_ITA=Italy, LOC_SPA=Spain, LOC_EUR=Europe. Map cities to their country (e.g. Budapest->LOC_HUN).
3. NEW ENTITIES: If an entity is NOT in the lists above, generate a NEW ID using these patterns:
   - Actors: A<number> (Start from A18)
   - Locations: LOC_<3-LETTER-CODE> (e.g. LOC_USA)
   - Processes: P<number> (e.g. P21)
   - Charging Stations: EVC-<year>-<number>
   - Materials: MAT_<number>
4. ENTITY MERGING: If you see variations of a name (e.g. 'Germany' and 'DE'), use the SAME Canonical ID.

Entity types: Actor, Location, ChargingStation, Process, Material, Risk, MaintenanceEvent, TestReport, IncidentReport, AuditFinding
Relationship types: LOCATED_IN, EXECUTED_BY, UNDERGOES, SUPPLIES, USES_MATERIAL, TESTED_BY, MAINTAINED_BY, RELATED_TO, MITIGATES, CAUSED_BY, DETECTED_IN

OUTPUT FORMAT (JSON):
You MUST output ONLY a valid JSON object matching exactly this schema, with no markdown formatting or backticks:
{
  "entities": [
    { "entity_type": "Actor", "canonical_id": "A1", "properties": { "name": "Steel Supplier Alpha" } }
  ],
  "relationships": [
    { "from_type": "Actor", "from_id": "A1", "relationship_type": "LOCATED_IN", "to_type": "Location", "to_id": "LOC_GER", "properties": {} }
  ]
}
